title: Li Shimin
subtitle: Taizong of Tang and a shaper of capital institutions
shortSummary: Li Shimin's courtly, educational and religious institutional context helps explain why Chang'an became a meeting point for different networks of knowledge and belief.
curatorialDescription: The museum does not make the emperor the sole protagonist of a three-tradition story; it places him within institutional resources, urban space and negotiation among traditions.
This figure record provides historical context. Specific edicts, institutional ties and later images require separate citations.
researchNote: Alpha entry; official-history editions, edict locators and evidence for ties among monasteries, Daoist institutions and schools remain to be itemised.
